# Relative-sized flat lines

Original controls generated by `tools/relative_flat_lines_fixture.py` from this
repository's original flat-line fixture. No corpus content is included. The
source and native reference PDF hashes are recorded in `reference.json`;
regenerate the PDF with `tools/export-reference.ps1` and measurements with
`tools/record_relative_flat_lines.py`.

All ten pages anchor a 2pt red line at (144pt, 144pt). Pages 1–6 apply a positive
percentage to the nonzero axis: horizontal/page/50%, vertical/margin/25%, rotated
horizontal/margin/50%, rotated vertical/page/30%, then horizontal and vertical
lines whose saved outer frame doubles the internal shape extent. Pages 7–8 size
the originally zero axis (height/page/25% and width/page/25%); pages 9–10 size both
axes to 25% of the margins. The final four controls become diagonal in the reference application.

The relative dimensions replace the saved frame dimensions before rotation.
They do not scale the physical pen. A collapsed axis stays zero only when no
positive relative size replaces it. The line preset has a unit path grid, so
assigning its resolved physical frame avoids division by the saved zero extent.
This is consistent with the existing relative-size behavior and establishes no
reference/spec divergence. The original frame/XML remains unchanged on export.

The browser test compares native saturated-red ink bounds within 1pt, selects
the actual rotated/diagonal strokes, and checks editing, exact no-edit/undo ZIP
preservation, unrelated-part preservation and edited reopening. The native
reference measures at 0.25pt per pixel. This extends the no-wrap page/margin
relative-sizing subset; it does not enable additional reference bases, wrapping
modes, zero-area groups, ordinary zero-sized pictures or point-sized lines.
